content:
The realistic simulated-agent trial completed on the RTX 5080 with the unchanged STEP1 implementation. Request-order prefetch was close to ARC; live-semantic prefetch was slower overall and worse for background requests in this one run. Real scoring and transfers occurred, but natural admission exposed only one or two blocks at a time, with no competing eligible sessions or constrained ranking. This does not demonstrate semantic selection value or a capacity benefit. No extra GPU experiment or workload retuning followed.

| Arm | Completed | Release→first-token p50 ms | Mean ms | Load elapsed s | Output tokens/s | Mean ITL ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Project ARC demand |45/45|2740.734|4400.293|39.615|82.394|32.806|
| ARC + request-order |45/45|2749.335|4401.796|39.662|82.295|32.876|
| ARC + live semantic |45/45|3147.689|4715.632|41.963|77.783|33.913|

Each arm generated3264 tokens. Throughput divides all completed tokens by first intended arrival→last completion; ITL divides first-to-last stream receipt spans by3219 token intervals. Semantic throughput was5.6% lower and elapsed5.9% longer than ARC. Single fixed-order runs have no repetition/noise estimate or significance claim. Closed-loop agent arrivals depend on completion plus private waits, so scheduling and cache histories differ across arms. These are product-level observations, not a matched-arrival causal estimate of the scoring component alone. No p95 (fewer than frozen100 observations). All arms missed the assistant-chosen1000ms TTFT SLO on31/45 requests, including12/12 background requests; zero failures/OOMs/preemptions.

| Arm | Agent p50 release-TTFT ms (33 requests) | Background p50 ms (12) | Background mean ITL ms (1140 intervals) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ARC |1699.347|7228.261|31.478|
| Request-order |1717.642|7220.355|31.527|
| Semantic |1683.970|8145.967|33.910|

Actual-submit p50 TTFT was2739.906/2748.526/3147.331ms. Release lateness ranged0.15–2.22ms across arms; intended-release times include it. Requests with another output stream spanning release:41/45,41/45,43/45. These client stream overlaps are not GPU busy measurements. All consumed speculative jobs occurred after background requests had finished; background interference here reflects the complete running product/capture/queueing workload, not simultaneous background decode at those late prefetch handoffs. Every request's timing, release realization, overlap and output digest is in measurements.csv and evidence/*-analysis.json.

| Arm | D2H MiB / admitted blocks | Demand H2D MiB | Speculative H2D MiB | Consumed blocks / requests | Ready-before-release consumed MiB | Unused MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ARC |24.75 /11|38.25|0|0 /0|0|0|
| Request-order |24.75 /11|22.50|18.00|7 /4|11.25|2.25|
| Semantic |24.75 /11|15.75|15.75|7 /5|15.75|0|

Both prefetch arms completed5 speculative jobs. Request-order staged8 blocks; one abandoned session's block expired unused, and one consumed2-block job became ready57.5ms after release. Semantic staged7 blocks, all later consumed and ready before release. On-time consumed coverage of the27 returning initial prefixes was only0.130%/0.182% (same8640MiB logical returning-prefix denominator). These are actual-byte coverage fractions, not full-context delivery. All consumed prefixes were partial and used real GPU splice:15.75MiB each. **Native adoption count was zero in every arm**, despite being enabled in both prefetch arms. This trial does not extend the prior oracle's native-adoption performance evidence.

Live production query capture ran at middle layer18, stride1, with1179 callback invocations; sampled tensor provenance shows fresh real queries, and ARC's manager received1040 actual score-EMA folds. Five nonempty semantic nominations used7 finite causal/fresh key observations; availability timestamps were no later than decision and ages within1000ms. Every nomination had one eligible session, hence zero constrained multi-candidate decisions. Semantic scoring callback thread CPU164.37ms/wall168.35ms and EMA fold CPU4.75ms/wall6.23ms are component observations, not total overhead; query dispatch, GPU scoring, scheduler/serialization and RPC costs remain in end-to-end results. Production's baseline empty nomination work was preserved:1163 empty events among1168 decisions. Semantic log size1.68MB vs0.68MB ARC/0.88MB request-order. This branch-specific product logging is a limitation; the optimizer was not used to hide it.

All135 requests had identical exact input/output token lists by request identity across arms. All once-captured prompt keys were complete, group0;6024 native SHA256/pickle chain recurrences per arm recomputed correctly after the first block, plus4377 repeated-prefix identity checks per arm. A driver omission left PYTHONHASHSEED unset: fresh engines intentionally choose random root hash salts, so all cross-server native digest byte comparisons differ. Root salts were not logged and first-block hashes cannot be independently recomputed. Exact canonical token chains and within-engine native identities match; this is the disclosed substitute for the frozen cross-arm native-byte check, not a claim that native bytes matched. No rerun was added to obtain identical salts.

Every consumed speculative job passed actual ordered-prefix membership, staged physical destination IDs, successful CUDA H2D completion before staging readiness/splice,36-layer real CUDA copy, same-default-stream ordering, completion event acknowledgment, official allocation→worker destination-ID checks and cleanup. Request-usable acknowledgments came after release (simple76–1313ms; semantic68–401ms), distinct from earlier stage-ready and worker host prepare-attention receipts. These host receipts are not kernel-completion times. Demand restore jobs succeeded. Full KV tensors were not independently bitwise dumped; cancellation expiry was observed organically, not fault-injected. The first offline validator wrongly compared a sorted transfer-record key list to chain order; corrected membership-vs-order analysis passed without changing logs or rerunning GPU. Initial failed validator receipt is retained.

Configuration was frozen before valid runs: cached **Qwen3-4B** (not Qwen3.5), dense BF16 TP1/block16,640-block1440MiB GPU pool,448MiB DRAM (199 usable blocks),192-block staging cap inside the640 pool, maxseq3/maxlen8192, ARC threshold2, soft retention off, owned_reclaimable. No qualification requests, resets, downloads, CUDA build, semantic retention or optimization changes. Actual sampled peak staging2 blocks (4.5MiB), referenced581/582/577 blocks; pool samples consistent, allocation failures zero. Staging submission→release byte-time lower bounds0/26.00/20.17MiB·s. Torch startup-including peak allocation about9.20GiB; fixed pool occupancy and preallocated VRAM are different quantities. No VRAM capacity reduction is claimed. Real source protection exists only in prefetch arms; whole-run D2H was nonzero and is included.

The synthetic natural-language/code trace has6 sessions,6 turns except one abandonment after3 completions, plus12 open-loop background requests. Initial past contexts2048/2304/2560 tokens were truncated once; growing dialogue appends actual completed outputs and released tool results. Background prompt is synthetic repetition/truncation to768 tokens; output64 agent/96 background. Private waits75–2400ms, future contents and abandonment remain in the load generator. Hints expose completed initial prefix/session metadata, fixed250ms policy estimate and pending-only250ms refresh up to2s. No release waits for hint acknowledgment. Request-order sent115 hints, semantic113; most found GPU-resident or DRAM-unavailable prefixes. The API has no cancellation endpoint: stop refresh on observed cancellation and allow existing leases to expire.

One initial ARC launch failed before completing any request because the task driver omitted required campaign_provenance. It is preserved under results/failed-arc-provenance and excluded from the table. Task-only repair passed CPU contract/actual connector validator checks and was refrozen; production bytes and workload unchanged. Valid model lifecycles total176.0 seconds; including the failed launch, see evidence/lifecycle.json. This is driver lifecycle wall time including model startup/shutdown, not measured GPU busy time.

Evidence: evidence/frozen.json and prepared.json (source/runtime/model/input/config pins), measurements.json plus measurements.csv (all requests), validity.json (chain/transfer gates and per-job timings), *-analysis.json (scores/events), results/*/raw.json.gz and server*.log.gz (lossless originals; compression.json round-trip hashes), driver-repair.md, baseline-analysis-frozen.json. Runtime remains the recovered authoritative Python subset with precompiled wheel additions, not an exact historical Git tree. No production code patch/commit/push was made by this trial. CPU candidate verification is separate and is recorded in candidate/REPORT.md after this baseline analysis freeze. Final process/custody/storage handback is evidence/cleanup.json and storage-handback.json; cleanup is only complete when those receipts exist.
